scope: Official sources for exact observation and publication timestamp recovery; no invented clocks

sources.finding: The current daily KRX ingestion preserves the trading date and collection evidence, not a per-row first-publication clock.
sources.action: Do not copy the trading-date close or API request time into an exact first-publication field. A release timestamp must be backed by the relevant official record.

sources.finding: DEXKOUS underlying observations are defined as New York noon buying rates.
sources.action: Convert source-defined noon by observation date with America/New_York DST rules. This is not a publication timestamp.

sources.finding: Some dated DDP availability notices have explicit timestamps and a dated H.10 table with values.
sources.action: Match release date, observation date and Korean won value; archive both notice and table. No fixed scheduled release clock.

sources.finding: Monthly date-filtered RSS provides publisher-reported pubDate. Existing official value documents can be joined by article ID and registration date.
sources.action: Match article and parsed observation/value. 323 months, 12390 notices inspected; 3724 existing value documents matched. This does not establish the first publication by any institution.

sources.finding: Release schedule and revision notices do not establish exact clocks for every daily observation. Treasury input quotes are described as approximately 15:30 ET.
sources.action: Do not turn approximate quote times or release schedules into exact historical timestamps. Preserve vintage dates separately.

sources.finding: Official daily spot history provides dates and values, without per-observation exact publication clocks in the inspected response.
sources.action: Keep exact clocks NULL when not evidenced. Do not substitute WTI futures settlement time for daily spot assessments.

sources.finding: Official daily history contains DATE/OPEN/HIGH/LOW/CLOSE, not individual publication timestamps. Historical dissemination end times have changed.
sources.action: Do not assign one current close/dissemination clock to all history. Timestamped official data would require separate verification and access.
